body.value:
저자:  Kyeong Tae Kim and Jae Young Choi

출판지: PATTERN RECOGNITION

논문제목:  Triple-branch Attention Network with Multiscale Facial Region Feature Selection for Facial Emotion Recognition

Abstract

This paper proposes new and novel “Triple-branch attention network (TriBAN)”, which selects and integrates key attention features based on multiple-scale facial regions for improved facial expression recognition (FER). The proposed TriBAN consists of three main branches: global branch, large local branch, and small local branch. The aim of global branch is to capture the overall characteristics of facial image. In addition, the large local branch is equipped with attention components within each regional area to filter out irrelevant regions, addressing occlusion and pose variations, and simultaneously capturing discriminant attention features, while the small local branch enhances the robustness of edge information and upscales feature size through pixel shuffling, enabling it to capture subtle expression changes in the generated small regions. In each aforementioned branch, discriminative features are adaptively chosen, and graph convolutional network is effectively used for integrating the selected features by considering their structural relationships. Extensive and comparative experiments on three wild FER datasets, namely RAF-DB, AffectNet, and FERplus, showed that the proposed TriBAN achieves better or comparable FER performances, compared to other recently developed FER methods. Our method outperformed FER approaches using ResNet18 as the backbone and showed slightly lower performance than ViT-based algorithms but achieved more than twice the inference speed.

저자: A. Yeong Han; Kwang Moo Yi; Kyeong Tae Kim; Jae Young Choi

출판지: IEEE ACCESS

논문제목:  Hierarchical Feature Attention Learning Network for Detecting Object and Discriminative Parts in Fine-Grained Visual Classification

논문링크: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10854460

Abstract

This paper proposes a novel hierarchical feature attention learning network for improved fine-grained visual classification (FGVC). Existing fine-grained classification methods rely heavily on attention mechanisms to differentiate minute details of similar objects. These mechanisms often assume that critical locations have a similar scale and are uniquely localizable, which is not always accurate. For instance, the size of a bird may vary across images, and the color of its beak might only be significant for species identification when its wing and tail colors are specific. This paper addresses this limitation by proposing a so-called hierarchical feature attention learning network, which initially focuses on the target object within the image, followed by multi-headed attention to identify key discriminative locations (patches). Especially, we develop a novel hierarchical attention approach that appropriately reduces misleading attentions by considering the object’s size for capturing correct attention parts. In addition, the proposed multi-headed attention allows for examining more complementary attention parts to identify the most discriminative features. Further, our framework is implemented as an architectural constraint, eliminating the need for object or part-level annotations in a weakly supervised detection manner. We conducted extensive and comparative experiments on three benchmark datasets: NABirds, CUB-200, and Oxford 102 Flower. The results demonstrate that our proposed hierarchical attention approach provides a robust and efficient solution for improved FGVC. Specifically, our method achieved a top-1 accuracy increase of approximately 93.0%, 92.7%, and 99.4% on the CUB-200-2011, NABirds, and Oxford 102 Flower benchmarks, respectively.
